mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25%, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates strengthening economic demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances following a sustained GDPC1 increase, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a UNRATE increase > 0.5%, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.1 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals supply-side weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects dim.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances following a significant INDPRO decrease, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% in a month signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer-driven sectors benefit.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a significant RSAFS increase, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.5% in a month, the real interest rate becomes more negative, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors seek higher returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following the described conditions, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 300,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth prospects improve.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 300,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances following the described conditions, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months indicates strengthening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances following a sustained HOUST increase, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.
